commenti.body: The film or the series. I saw the film first when it came out thought it was really engrossing, profound and touching, the series being episodic seemed disjointed probably just me though as it was the same story 😂.

I've only seen the TV series. I'd suggest it was an incredibly personal film for Bergman. It's not autobiographical, but there are autobiographical elements. Example - the more explicitly autobiographical film Sunday's Children (screenplay by Bergman) features the character of Uncle Carl played by the same actor who plays Uncle Carl in Fanny And Alexander! Uncle Carl is just one of the characters taken from Bergman's childhood memories. 

I'm not an expert on Bergman and his life (just a regular viewer), but it seems to me Fanny And Alexander is a summation of his entire world view - and answer to his life long quest for meaning, for truth, and for God. I say 'answer', but there is great mystery in the Fanny And Alexander universe. The joyous twist is that the mystery is not a reason for depression or nihilism (as it is in some of his earlier films). Mystery here is the source of beauty, the source of meaning, and a reason to wonder at the world. The film encourages us towards a state of wonder.

I love Fanny and Alexander but have at best a superficial understanding of Bergman's overall filmography and life story. He apparently once said that there is more of him in the bishop than in Alexander -- I think he meant his controlling nature as a director.  That quote stuck with me.  [This write-up](https://www.ingmarbergman.se/en/production/fanny-and-alexander-0) has some interesting background.

If you have Criterion Channel, there's a good behind-the-scenes documentary about the making of the movie.

>his discontent with his authoritarian, religious stepfather, and his eventual anger towards God seem like the exact formative experiences that would influence the themes covered in Bergman’s filmography.


There's an interview from the early 70s on the dick cavett show where ingmar confirms this is true, minor caveat less anger to god and more just irreverence


You are spot on there
